drivingQuestion: Must the one sounding intend on behalf of the hearer?
outcomeNote: the refutation of R' Zeira is dismissed; the question stands

segments.he: דִּלְמָא אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא מִתְעַסֵּק, תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי מִתְעַסֵּק.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this argument. «Perhaps» one can explain that «since» the «first clause» of the mishna «taught» the halakha with regard to «one who acts unawares, the latter clause also taught» the halakha with regard to «one who acts unawares.» If so, no inference may be drawn from here to the case of one who sounds the shofar for himself, with no intention of doing so for others.

moves.summary: the latter clause echoes the first; no inference against R' Zeira
moves.about: the latter clause says 'acts unawares' only because the first clause did; no inference to one sounding for himself

edges.cueHe: דלמא איידי דתנא רישא מתעסק, תנא סיפא נמי מתעסק
edges.about: the latter clause says 'acts unawares' only because the first clause did; no inference to one sounding for himself
